drug_class: Anti-VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitor) / Ophthalmic biologic
purpose: Ranibizumab-eqrn is used to treat certain eye conditions that can cause vision loss, including wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic macular edema, and other retinal blood vessel problems. It helps protect your vision and in some cases can even improve it. Your eye doctor will determine if this medication is right for your specific condition.
how_it_works: In some eye diseases, abnormal blood vessels grow in the back of the eye and leak fluid, which damages your vision. This medicine blocks a protein called VEGF that causes those abnormal blood vessels to grow and leak. By blocking that protein, the medicine helps stop the leaking and prevents further damage to your eyesight.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include eye redness, eye pain or discomfort, floaters (spots or specks in your vision), increased pressure in the eye, and temporary blurred vision after the injection. You may also notice small bleeding at the injection site on the eye surface, which usually goes away on its own.
warnings: Call your doctor right away if you notice sudden vision changes, increased eye pain, severe redness, or increased sensitivity to light, as these could be signs of a serious eye infection called endophthalmitis. There is also a small risk of stroke or serious blood clots, so tell your doctor if you have a history of heart disease or stroke. This medication is given only by injection into the eye by a trained eye doctor and should never be self-administered.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection directly into the eye by your eye doctor, usually once a month to start. After the first few months, your doctor may space out the injections based on how your eye is responding — sometimes every 2 to 3 months. Your doctor will create a schedule that is best for your individual condition.
